messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike detected in /v1/generate P95/P99 latency and elevated 502/504 rate. Aggregated window 5m. p95=420ms -> 1.8s, p99=2.1s -> 14.6s, 5xx rate at 6.4% :rotating_light: https://metrics.internal/redwood/alerts/alert-1234
Mia (oncall): I'm on it. hitting the runtime channel and pulling deploy id. anyone seeing errors in traces?
Rob (runtime): yeah seeing long tail on multiplexed worker pods. KVs look fine but connection handshakes are taking long.
Sree (eng-sre): incident-bot showed recent deploy at 1719999400 -> rollout v2026.03.15-7f8c. Can we confirm if the new image toggles multiplex config?
Mia (oncall): Confirmed. rollout v2026.03.15-7f8c enabled multiplexing=true by default.
Rob (runtime): stack traces show repeated `StreamReadTimeout` in transport layer. sample log from pod inference-87d:
```
2026-03-15T14:22:10Z ERROR transport: read timeout after 12000ms
2026-03-15T14:22:10Z WARN  kvcache: miss for prefix abc123
2026-03-15T14:22:10Z ERROR grpc: conn reset: EOF
```

Mia (oncall): current impact: approx 18% of requests in US-west experiencing >5s latencies, overall 5xx up. Customer-facing telemetry flagged increased API error pages. Tara, any incoming tickets?
Tara (support): Yes, a handful of premium customers seeing 504s via our integrations. Logged 3 pager warnings. Customers affected include `analytics-bench` and `docflow`. Escalating to account leads.
Sree (eng-sre): quick mitigation options: 1) toggle multiplexing=false and restart worker set, 2) rollback to previous image (v2026.03.12-3b2a). Which is faster?
Rob (runtime): toggling config requires rolling restart and may still hit rewarm/warmup issues. Rollback is single step with deploy-bot and should restore previous steady-state quickly.
Mia (oncall): leaning rollback. @deploy-bot can you run a revert to v2026.03.12-3b2a on production with zero-downtime strategy? Confirm ETA.
deploy-bot: `@Mia (oncall) rollback initiated: revert-to=v2026.03.12-3b2a, rollout-id=rb-1719999999, strategy=canary(10%->100% over 5m), started.`
Mia (oncall): executing. I'll watch logs and traces, marking channel as incident.
Rob (runtime): adding quick watch queries:
```
# query p99 latency for /v1/generate
SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 99) FROM requests WHERE route='/v1/generate' SINCE 1m
```

Sree (eng-sre): also disabling multiplex backpressure feature on canary pods as a precaution via feature-flag `mux_backpressure=false`.
Mia (oncall): deploy-bot reports canary at 10% done. watching error rate.
deploy-bot: `canary step complete: 10% -> 100% in progress (expected finish ~ 4m).`
Mia (oncall): error rate dropping on canary nodes — 5xx on canary = 0.4%. routing remaining traffic now.
Rob (runtime): rolling to 100% complete. I see p95/p99 dropping in traces.
Mia (oncall): New metrics: p95=380ms, p99=760ms, 5xx overall back to ~0.6%.
Tara (support): Notifying affected customers with an update: root cause suspected regression from multiplex config in recent deploy; rollback in progress, monitoring.
Jules (product): tagging incident as P2 for now. Any data loss?
Mia (oncall): no data loss observed, only timeouts/5xx. We'll confirm full window but initial customer impact limited to request failures and retries.
Sree (eng-sre): post-rollback checklist: pin model-serving image, revert feature-flag defaults, add integration test for multiplex handshake latency.
Rob (runtime): leaving a live snippet on runbook: `if p99 > 2s after deploy then abort rollout and rollback` — already added an automated alert tweak.
incident-bot: INCIDENT: rollback completed at 1720000120, status=resolved (service degraded -> restored).
Mia (oncall): handing off to Sree for postmortem — Sree you're the owner?
Sree (eng-sre): taking postmortem. I'll schedule a triage doc and invite runtime, deploy and support. Assigning follow-up: add a canary e2e test that exercises multiplex handshakes under high-concurrency.
Tara (support): I'll follow up with affected accounts with a timeline and offer temporary quota/burst to smooth retries.
Mia (oncall): Handoff complete. Next oncall @Rob at 16:00 UTC — leaving notes in oncall doc. Thank you all :heart:
Rob (runtime): TL;DR: post-deploy multiplexing default caused transport handshake stalls under heavy concurrent short requests -> p99/timeouts spike -> immediate rollback restored baseline. Postmortem owner Sree, comms owner Tara.
incident-bot: Closing incident thread. Reference: INC-2026-0456.
